fix(types): public declarations name no Node types (rich-types-42o) (#236)

* fix(types): public declarations name no Node types (rich-types-42o)

`ConsoleEnvironment.env`, `DetectColorOptions.env`, `RenderToStringOptions.env`
and `TerminalHost.env` were typed `NodeJS.ProcessEnv`, which the emitted .d.ts
carried verbatim; a project with no @types/node and skipLibCheck off failed on
them with `Cannot find namespace 'NodeJS'`. They now share `Env` (src/core/env.ts),
a read-only map from string to optional string that `process.env` satisfies
without a cast.

test/seam/browser-types.test.ts emits the declarations into a temp node_modules
and type-checks every non-node/ entry by its published specifier with
`types: []`; it fails with the five original errors on the old source.

Co-Authored-By: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>

* test(types): the NodeJS probe imports every entry; fixtures name Env (rich-types-42o)

Review pass (high) on #236:
- The guard probe imported nothing, so Node types leaked through a symlinked
  peer's reference directive left it failing for the wrong reason. It now
  imports every browser entry first; reproduced with a scratch peer: old probe
  exit 2, new probe exit 0.
- Consumer tsconfig pins noUncheckedSideEffectImports rather than trusting
  TypeScript's default to make an unresolved entry an error.
- ambient-process.test.ts draws the airlock through isBehindNodeAirlock.
- Test fixtures standing in for the public API annotate Env, not ProcessEnv.

Co-Authored-By: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>
